title: feat(app-shell): Studio's nav editor offers every nav item type the spec declares (objectui#11790)
body:
Fixes #11790

Clause-②: no. Nothing is added to the package entry: no export, prop, `@object-ui/types` member or `packages/i18n` key. `StudioNavItemInspector` gains one internal prop, `packageId`; that component is exported from its module for tests only and is not re-exported from the package index (`package.json` exports only `.`). The new copy is rows of the designer's own unexported string tables in `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, under `engine.inspector.appNav.*` only.

Implemented by the os-dev agent of seat `domain:ui#1` under claim comment 6049484420, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01DrKzdPdyLLBW3qpZ4vtk7z`. Step 1 of the card only: no create flows (those are objectui#11823).

## What changes

In a writable package, *Add nav item* still appends an `object` entry and selects it. The Studio nav-item inspector (`StudioNavItemInspector`) now opens with a **Type** choice that lists every member of the installed spec's `NavigationItemSchema`. Picking a type rewrites the entry for that type, and the inspector shows that type's target picker.

- **The type list is the spec's.** `NAV_ENTRY_TYPES` (in `inspectors/nav-target.ts`) is a Record keyed by the spec-derived `NavigationItemType`, so the compiler refuses a missing or extra member. The runtime pins read the union's discriminants off the installed spec.
- **A change of type** (`retypedNavEntry`) keeps what describes the entry: its id, label, icon, order, badge, badge variant, `visible`, `requiredPermissions`, `requiresObject` and `requiresService`. It drops what the entry opened. A separator keeps only `id` and `order`. A group is born with `children: []`, which its member requires. Children stay on `object` and `group`, and an entry holding children may change only to one of those two.
- **Targets come from the package.** Page, dashboard, report, action, doc and book pickers read `client.list(TYPE, { packageId })` together with `client.listDrafts({ packageId, type })`, the same published-plus-draft union the pillar's object list uses. The pickers leave out a confirmed record page (`isStaticPageOption`) and a confirmed object-bound action, because the nav runs global actions only. A draft header carries no body, so a draft-only row is kept. A `component` entry picks from the console's component registry (`listAppComponents`). A `url` entry is typed and has an *Open in* select. An emptied picker removes the key and never writes an empty string, so the entry becomes unbound again.
- **The save path is objectui#11776's, unchanged.** `doNavSave`, `navPayloadOf` and `NAV_TARGET_READS` are untouched; that table already had a row for every target-bearing type. An unbound entry of any type stays on the canvas and is left out of the save. A `group` and a `separator` open nothing, so they are sent.
- **Rail and canvas.** `KIND_ICON` gains glyphs for `url`, `component` and `doc`. Those rows open no design surface (`resolveSurface` binds none), so they stay disabled. The nav canvas no longer offers inline rename on a separator card, because a separator has no label and one written there is refused at save.
- **Control:** *Link to object* is the same select, writes the same entry, and still shows on an `object` entry and on an untyped one (what an object unbind leaves).

## Measured before building (dispatch hypotheses)

- **The spec's type list.** Read from installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 by walking `NavigationItemSchema`'s discriminated-union options: object, dashboard, page, url, report, action, component, doc, separator, group. Triage's direction named seven of them. The spec also declares `action`, `component` and `doc` as members. Nothing marks a member as non-addable (the separator schema is a module-private const, but it is a member of the union the schema parses), so all ten are offered, per the ruling "offer exactly those". This is a reading on 17.7.0. The pins in `nav-target.navEntryTypes-11790.test.ts` re-derive it against whatever spec is installed.
- **H1, partly right.** `AppNavCanvas`'s `addItem` births `{ id, type: 'object' }`. The Studio's inspector is `StudioNavItemInspector` in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, not `AppNavInspector`. `AppNavInspector` is the Setup app editor's inspector (`registerMetadataInspector('app', AppNavInspector)`), and its own Type select already offers six types.
- **H2, falsified for the Studio.** `StudioNavItemInspector` edited only object binding. On an existing page, dashboard, url or group entry, it showed *Link to object* with an empty value and the object hint. Picking an object there wrote `type: 'object'` and `objectName` and kept the old target key. Measured on a page entry: the result `{ id, type: 'object', label, pageName, objectName }` is refused by `NavigationItemSchema` with `unrecognized_keys` `pageName`. The per-type pickers remove that path.
- **H3, right.** `resolveSurface` binds page, object, dashboard, report and action. A new `group` renders as a section header. `url`, `component` and `doc` render as disabled rows. A new `separator` renders as an empty disabled row with the generic glyph. That is objectui#11791's defect, which is left to its card and untouched here.

## Why the type choice is in the inspector, not a menu on the button

The order offered both routes. The inspector route was measured as the better one:

1. `AppNavCanvas`'s *Add nav item* is shared with the Setup app editor, whose `AppNavInspector` Type select is its chooser. One behaviour in both editors.
2. A type choice in the inspector also changes an existing entry's type. A menu on the button cannot.
3. The suites that drive *Add nav item* (Studio and Setup) click it and expect an appended entry. A Radix menu trigger opens on pointerdown, so a menu would have rewritten those suites, some of them in seat 3's autosave area, for no gain in behaviour.

The choice is a set of radio inputs in a fieldset, not a select. On an `object` entry, the inspector's one combobox is still the object picker.

## Tests

New pins:

- `inspectors/nav-target.navEntryTypes-11790.test.ts` (pure):
  - `NAV_ENTRY_TYPES` equals the installed spec's union discriminants.
  - `navTypeAcceptsChildren` equals the spec's own answer for each type.
  - Each retype, once bound, parses with `NavigationItemSchema`. Unbound, it carries no key the member refuses.
  - The base keys survive a retype. The base set is read off the spec's member shapes, not off a second list.
  - A separator retype has exactly the separator member's keys.
- `studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.navItemTypes-11790.test.tsx`:
  - The inspector offers exactly the spec's types.
  - Each target-bearing type picks its target and writes an entry that parses with `NavigationItemSchema`. That covers page, dashboard, report, action, component and doc. A url is typed, and a book alone is also a target.
  - The pickers offer this package's published and draft items. A record page, an object-bound action and another package's page are not offered.
  - Clearing a target removes the key, and `navPayloadOf` then leaves the entry out.
  - A separator has no Label field and is sent. A group is born empty and is sent.
  - An entry holding children may change only to `object` or `group`.
  - Control: *Link to object*.
  - Pillar level:
    - *Add nav item* offers exactly the spec's types.
    - A dashboard, a separator and an empty group are sent. Each save is parsed by an `AppSchema` double, and every one is accepted. An unbound url is left out and stays on the canvas.
    - After *Done*, the rail shows the new entries.

Four existing inspector suites pass the new `packageId` prop: `navItemInspector`, `navItemInspectorLabel-11196`, `navItemInspectorLabelMaps-11148` and `standardNavEntries-11201`. Nothing else in them changed.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full test farm are left to CI. The added gates were derived by hand from objectui's `package.json`. This repo has no `dispatch-gates.mjs`, so they were picked by what reads the changed files: three `vi-mock` gates for the new mocking suite, two i18n gates for the new rows, `spec-symbols` for the spec-keyed table, `icon-record-names` for the icon table, and changeset presence.

**Reverse check.** The fix was committed first. The script then reverted `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` alone to the base `1e1f09e` and re-ran the pins named "offers exactly the". The predicted direction was that no type choice exists. Observed:

- `offers exactly the types the spec declares…`: `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an accessible element with the role "radio"`.
- `"Add nav item" offers exactly the spec's nav item types`: `Unable to find role="group" and name "Type"`.
- Result: `Tests 2 failed | 18 skipped`.

The file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` from a trap. Proof of the restore: its hash equals the HEAD blob `2fe2efe6`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Real-browser reading.** This used a dev-only harness that is not committed. A console Vite page on a private port mounted `InterfacesPillar` over an in-memory `/api/v1/meta` fetch double, which parses every app save with `AppSchema`. The harness was driven in Chromium (`/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, 1440×900) with Playwright.

- After *Add nav item*, the Type choice offered object, page, dashboard, report, url, action, component, doc, group and separator, with *Object* checked.
- The Page picker offered `home` and `draft_page`. The record page and the other package's page were not offered.
- The Action picker offered `sync_all` but not the object-bound `close_task`.
- The Component picker offered the four screens the app-shell registers.
- An unbound url entry was left out of the save, and that save was accepted.
- The author then added one entry of every type: dashboard, page, report, action, component, doc, group, separator, url and object. Both saves were accepted. The final navigation carried all twelve entries, each in its member's shape.
- After *Done*:
  - The rail showed every entry. Dashboard, page, report, action and object rows were enabled.
  - Component, doc and url rows were disabled under their own glyphs, and the group showed as a section header.
  - The separator was an empty disabled row, which is objectui#11791.
- No page errors.

## Acceptance notes

None of these is filed.

- **Setup's `AppNavInspector` offers six of the spec's ten types.** It lacks action, component, doc and separator. That is an enhancement in another editor, not a defect class. Carrier: none.
- **Nesting entries under a group from Studio is a follow-up.** This editor edits top-level entries only (`navigation[i]`), and the canvas does not nest, so a group is added flat with `children: []`.
- **The doc picker offers declared books, not the package's implicit book (the package id).** A doc alone opens in its own book context, so nothing is unreachable.
- **The separator's rail rendering is objectui#11791's.** It is unchanged here.
- **The commit trailers are the model-free pair AGENTS.md requires** (`Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by: Claude`). The harness's model-named variant was not used.

## Files

All files are in the claimed surface:

- `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: `StudioNavItemInspector` and its pickers, the call site's `packageId`, `KIND_ICON`, and icon imports. None of objectui#11785's strips is touched.
- `views/metadata-admin/inspectors/nav-target.ts`: `NAV_ENTRY_TYPES`, `isNavEntryType`, `navTypeAcceptsChildren` and `retypedNavEntry`. The `NAV_ITEM_TYPES` comment was corrected.
- `views/metadata-admin/previews/AppNavCanvas.tsx`: the separator rename guard and the `addItem` comment.
- `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`: new `engine.inspector.appNav.*` rows in en and zh.
- The tests beside these files.
- `.changeset/11790-nav-item-types.md` (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

`main` moved by one commit since the base: objectui#11840, which added rows to `i18n.ts`. A test merge of this branch with that `main` is clean. The merge queue rebuilds on the `main` it lands on.
